solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Two bottles of drink knocked back is a great achievement

parts.note: a magnum holds the equivalent of two standard 75cl wine bottles
O is a short form of 'of', as in o'clock

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is tipped up, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips

explanation.surface: Downing two bottles' worth of booze is quite a feat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like drinking slang but turns O and SUP round to give OPUS; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum opus is Latin for a 'great work', the masterpiece of a career.

clue.text: Mistakenly head into one during cover-up?

definitions.text: Mistakenly head into one during cover-up?

parts.words: Mistakenly head into one during cover-up?
parts.note: pulling on a jumper, one sometimes pushes one's head through the wrong opening, a sleeve hole

explanation.surface: Someone blunders into something while hushing up a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover-up' suggests a political scandal; here it is a garment being put on.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening in a garment through which the arm passes can be mistaken for the neck opening.

clue.text: Chap getting leg over proceeded gingerly

indicators.note: in a down clue 'over' turns the pieces upside down, so they read in reverse

parts.note: Des is a man's name, short for Desmond
the on side, or leg side, is a cricket field term for the batter's leg side

explanation.surface: A man gets a leg over a fence and moves cautiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reverses DES + ON (DESON) to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose forward is to move slowly and carefully, edging ahead like a probing animal.

clue.text: Girl without a bank, in a poor way?

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside, so the girl's name wraps around the letter

parts.note: Meg is a girl's name
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A girl with no bank account is badly off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here: MEG goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something scantily or inadequately, as with a thin, scant ration.

clue.text: Composition is safe with one duke who left unexpectedly

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
an means one

indicators.note: something done unexpectedly comes out differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of music is somehow tied to a safe and a duke who departed without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' rearranges WHO LEFT into THE WOLF; 'is' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Prokofiev's 1936 musical tale for children with a narrator, a famous orchestral work.

clue.text: Inferior rum that's lacking bottling

indicators.note: something bottling another holds it inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: shy of means short or lacking, as in 'two shy of a dozen'
rum is old slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Poor-quality rum, the kind not even worth bottling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink but is the old adjective for strange; 'that's lacking' is the phrase 'shy of', short of.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy goods are of poor quality, cheaply or badly made.

clue.text: Jumble sale in which flowers might be found

definitions.text: in which flowers might be found
definitions.note: a plural noun phrase for grassy places where wild flowers grow

indicators.note: a jumble is a muddle, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A jumble sale is a place where bunches of flowers might turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumble sale' reads as one British charity event, where donated goods are sold cheaply; 'Jumble' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Leas are meadows or grassland, where wild flowers commonly grow.

clue.text: One who exists to accumulate port

parts.note: someone who lives is, literally, a liver
to pool resources is to gather them together

explanation.surface: Someone who lives only to amass wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liver' is read as one who lives, not the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A major seaport city on the Mersey in north-west England.

clue.text: Volunteers advance south of area if necessary

indicators.note: in a down clue being south of something means coming below it, so the area letter goes first

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
a push is a military advance

explanation.surface: Reserve soldiers push forward south of the zone if they have to.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is the British army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'at a push' means only if forced to, with difficulty, if absolutely needed.

clue.text: Fellow cross about annual holiday

indicators.note: 'about' here means turned about, so these letters read backwards

parts.note: Sam is a man's name, a fellow
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A man gets cross about the yearly festive break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry' but is the letter X; 'about' turns SAM + X round.
explanation.definitionFit: Short form of Christmas, celebrated every year on 25 December.

clue.text: French school voluntarily pruning plant ruined by Vichy water

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the remaining letters are rearranged
pruning cuts parts away, so the plant's letters are removed from the word

parts.note: a lily is a flowering plant
eau is French for water, Vichy being a French spa town

explanation.surface: A gardener willingly prunes a plant that has been spoiled by spa water.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking L, I, L, Y out of VOLUNTARILY leaves VOUNTAR; 'ruined' turns that into ARTNOUV.
explanation.definitionFit: Art nouveau is a decorative style of around 1900, a movement of artists and designers.

clue.text: That one, contrary to expectation, turned the corner at last

indicators.note: the final letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Contrary to what was expected, someone finally rounded the corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' looks like part of the story but picks the last letter of the six words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic or dialect word meaning 'that one over there', pointing to something distant.

clue.text: Sporting event jockey announced by a lone supporter?

indicators.note: something announced is said out loud, so we want a word sounding like the jockey

parts.note: a jockey is a rider of racehorses
one cup of a bra is a single support, half the garment

explanation.surface: A racing jockey is introduced at a race by his only fan.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'lone supporter' is one half of a bra.
explanation.definitionFit: The biennial golf contest between Europe and the United States.

clue.text: Inventor, by proxy, getting high priest into branch of Buddhism

indicators.note: these pieces go into the Buddhist school, so it is split open around them

parts.note: Zen is a Japanese school of Buddhism
pp, per procurationem, is written when signing on another's behalf
Eli is the high priest in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: An inventor uses a stand-in to bring a senior cleric into a Buddhist sect.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is the abbreviation used when signing a letter on someone else's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin was the German who designed rigid airships.

clue.text: Cast kept full of euphoric feeling before a famous ballet

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are filled with the feeling, holding it inside
cast as in recast or thrown into new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a rush is a sudden surge of euphoria

explanation.surface: The performers were thrilled ahead of a famous ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the company of dancers but is the anagram signal, giving PETK; 'before' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stravinsky's 1911 ballet about a puppet brought to life, performed by the Ballets Russes.

clue.text: Darts away from this partial ricochet

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, so the answer lies inside it

explanation.surface: Darts that bounce off and fly away, a partial rebound.
explanation.walkthrough: The line darts players stand behind is a pub-game term worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is the line behind which a player stands to throw darts.

clue.text: Pomegranate syrup's not in pineapples

indicators.note: the word that follows is to be left out of the syrup

parts.note: grenadine is a red syrup made from pomegranates; the 's gives a plural ending

explanation.surface: Pomegranate cordial is not found in pineapples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pineapples' is old military slang for hand grenades, from their shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Pineapples is slang for hand bombs, whose segmented casing resembles the fruit.

clue.text: Agreement's in the bag, reportedly

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by speech, so the word sounds like the phrase

parts.note: items in a bag have been packed

explanation.surface: The deal is as good as done, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the bag' looks like 'certain', supporting the deal; it means packed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal deal or treaty between parties.

clue.text: Most of strong women are "birds", of a sort

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its last letter

parts.note: Amazons were a legendary race of women warriors
an are is a metric unit of area, a hundred square metres, symbol a

explanation.surface: Most powerful women are 'birds', in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birds' is British slang for women, but here means real birds; 'are' gives A, a metric unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazona is the genus of parrots from the Americas, so its members are a kind of bird.

clue.text: Hitler shot with both hands? That's sensational

indicators.note: something shot is shattered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left

explanation.surface: Hitler fired a gun with both hands, which caused a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like gunfire; it rearranges HITLER plus R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspenseful novel or film designed to excite, sensational entertainment.

clue.text: General groundswell?

indicators.note: ground up, as grain is, so these letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A broad upsurge of public feeling, or a heaving of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groundswell' reads as one word; split it into 'ground' (the anagram signal) and 'swell' (the definition).
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to grow bigger, to expand or increase in size.

clue.text: Enemies capturing area on central Admiralty Islands

indicators.note: the enemies take prisoners, so they wrap round the other letters

parts.note: foes are enemies

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Foes seize territory near the middle of a Pacific island group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admiralty Islands' looks like one name; 'central' picks R from Admiralty, and 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Faroes are a group of North Atlantic islands belonging to Denmark.

clue.text: Dead placed on forbidden altar frontal

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Dead placed on forbidden altar frontal' gives LATE after TABU, but the definition 'altar frontal' means TABULA, not TABULATE; the blog also could not justify it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Dead placed on forbidden altar frontal

clue.text: Middle of banana tree that's highly inflammable

indicators.note: the central letters of the word are taken

parts.note: a palm is a tropical tree

explanation.surface: The core of a banana tree burns very easily.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle two letters of BANANA give NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm is a jellied petrol used in incendiary weapons, so it burns fiercely.

clue.text: Small plug for a little while

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a mo is a moment

explanation.surface: A brief advertisement, just for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' is a piece of publicity, not a stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is a short promotional piece, a brief advertisement.

clue.text: Noted rendezvous at the end of superior and inferior routes?

definitions.text: Noted rendezvous at the end of superior and inferior routes?

parts.words: Noted rendezvous at the end of superior and inferior routes?
parts.note: the Scottish song has one taking the high road and the other the low road, meeting on its bonnie banks

explanation.surface: A famous meeting point at the end of upper and lower roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means set to music: the folk song 'The Bonnie Banks o' ...' with its high road and low road.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish lake is the destination of the high road and low road in the famous song.

clue.text: Part of dark-orange, round plant

indicators.note: turned round, so the picked letters read backwards
only a part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: Part of a dark-orange round plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' takes ARKO from dark-orange; 'round' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a vegetable plant whose green pods are cooked, also called ladies' fingers.

clue.text: Originally knew all the answers for Japanese exercises?

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A star pupil had all the answers to the Japanese drills from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Kata are set sequences of movements practised in karate and other martial arts.

clue.text: Affable stepson gets fine, working without approval

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters surround the approval
letters set working are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine on pencil grades
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: A friendly stepson is fined for working without permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' gives SOFTSPEN; 'without' means outside, not lacking; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone affable and mild speaks gently and quietly.
